candidates.label: candidate-1
candidates.text:
A moving average lets the state adjust to a new input while keeping part of its previous value. If the previous state is 10 and the new input is 20, keep 80% of the old state and add 20% of the input: 0.8 × 10 + 0.2 × 20 = 12.

This update follows $s_t = 0.8s_{t-1} + 0.2x_t$, where $s_t$ is the updated state, $s_{t-1}$ is the previous state and $x_t$ is the new input. This is a toy illustration, not a measured experiment.

candidates.label: candidate-2
candidates.text:
A moving average smooths incoming values by combining the previous state with the latest input. Here, each update retains 80% of the previous state and adds 20% of the new input.

For example, if the previous state is 10 and the new input is 20, the update is 0.8 × 10 + 0.2 × 20 = 12.

The recurrence is $s_t = 0.8s_{t-1} + 0.2x_t$. This is a numerical illustration, not a measured experiment.

candidates.label: candidate-3
candidates.text:
Think of the state as a running value that changes gradually as new inputs arrive. It keeps 80% of its previous value and takes 20% of the new input.

Starting from 10 with a new input of 20 gives 0.8 × 10 + 0.2 × 20 = 12.

The update rule is $s_t = 0.8s_{t-1} + 0.2x_t$. This illustrates the calculation; it is not a measured experiment.
